standard: Maintained experiments must make design provenance, bounded acceptance criteria, outcome, reproducibility, and exact revision-bound evidence explicit.

entries.question: Can Overcenter claim real work and deliver a self-contained byte-complete assignment to an empty disposable worker?
entries.claim: For the bounded proof workload, the claimed Work snapshot plus exact task bytes is sufficient for a no-checkout, no-network worker to produce candidate output that trusted authority can independently settle.
entries.contrast: Assign exact identity but require the worker to obtain source/input bytes through an ambient checkout or mount.
environment: Node.js from .node-version for the deterministic contract.
GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04 for the no-checkout worker and isolated network namespace.
success_criteria: A production SQLite kernel derives READY work and claims it at an exact revision.
The worker receives the claimed Work snapshot and all task-specific bytes in one immutable capsule.
The worker executes with no checkout, repository permission, execution capability, or outbound network namespace.
Missing or altered required bytes fail closed before execution.
Candidate bytes bind to the exact assignment digest, obligation, run, and claimed revision.
Trusted reconstruction and independent observation settle the same run DONE.

artifacts: GitHub Actions run 35488740731: exact-head hosted assignment capsule proof; deterministic contract, no-checkout worker, isolated network namespace, damaged-assignment controls, and trusted settlement all passed.

entries.interpretation: A positive result proves byte-complete assignment plumbing for the bounded workload; it does not make the worker authoritative for success or imply arbitrary toolchain portability.
non_claims: The Node runtime or Linux kernel are embedded in the assignment.
This is a general artifact distribution or confidential payload service.
Arbitrary provider mutation is authorized by the worker capsule.
Every future obligation already fits this proof packet.

design.note: The boundary and fail-closed criteria were committed on the experiment branch before the hosted proof result; later exact-head runs confirm the same bounded contract.

outcome.summary: Exact claimed work and task bytes were delivered to a no-checkout, no-network worker and independently settled by trusted authority.

entries.question: Can ClaimFact, ExecutionAuthorityFact, and EffectReservationFact safely collapse to Claim + Attempt while actually reducing machinery and preserving performance?
entries.claim: In the bounded recovery model, one Attempt clock cannot simultaneously rotate to fence stale workers and remain stable to represent an unresolved external mutation. A safe Claim + Attempt representation therefore recreates the missing dimension as execute/recover purpose plus unresolved-effect identity, preserving safety and throughput but not reducing writes or source surface.
entries.contrast: Keep semantic claim ownership, execution/recovery fencing, and unresolved external-effect reservation as distinct state dimensions.

design.note: The simplification hypothesis and acceptance thresholds were fixed before hosted confirmation, while the candidate shape was informed by prior production-code inspection and exploratory local modeling.

outcome.summary: The safe collapse preserved safety and met the performance bound but grew the bounded authority model from 88 to 107 SLOC (+21.6%) with unchanged representative durable-write counts. Both smaller single-clock variants fail: rotating the clock admits a successor while the prior external mutation remains unresolved; preserving it fails to fence stale authority.

environment: Node.js from .node-version for the executable differential.
Pinned Lean semantic oracle revision 39bd16a317bc2155a17b6674a5050adaf4295c90 for the universal two-clock necessity theorem.
No provider credential, database, or model is required for the deterministic experiment.
success_criteria: The safe candidate rejects stale authority after recovery fencing.
Recovery-only authority cannot execute a second unresolved external effect.
Replay-safe computation still requires proof that the prior containment domain terminated.
Representative durable-write counts are no worse than the legacy-shaped reference.
The safe candidate is smaller than the legacy-shaped reference by at least 5% SLOC for the proposed simplification to be supported.
If one Attempt clock rotates on recovery, the negative control demonstrates duplicate external-effect eligibility unless unresolved-effect state is tracked separately.
If one Attempt clock is preserved across recovery to retain mutation identity, the negative control demonstrates that stale execution authority remains accepted.
Median in-process effect-recovery transition time remains within 1.25x of the legacy-shaped reference over seven 200,000-transaction samples.
The pinned Lean oracle proves for arbitrary epoch types that authority rotation plus mutation-epoch persistence contradicts a single clock that remains aliased before and after recovery.

artifacts: GitHub Actions Merge gate run 35757238433, rerun attempt 2: exact-head candidate evidence PASS
authority-model-sloc: legacy 88, safe candidate 107, unsafe candidate 33
effect-recovery-throughput: 200000 iterations, legacy median 20.043804 ms, candidate median 15.031002 ms, ratio 0.749908
TLA+ transition kernel and resource-containment negative controls behaved as expected in run 35757238433
Production Rust worker confinement boundary PASS in run 35757238433
Proof PR #253 exact theorem head: Lean build and leanchecker declaration replay PASS

entries.interpretation: The negative result is about temporal factorization, not naming: claim lifetime, authority epoch, and mutation-uncertainty lifetime are not coextensive. A safe simplification must preserve those dimensions while reducing surrounding choreography rather than aliasing them into one clock.
non_claims: The in-process transition benchmark represents provider I/O, SQLite latency, or native executor overhead.
The Go computation executor should be retained or removed.
The present production implementation is globally minimal.
No alternative representation can reduce code while preserving the same independent temporal dimensions.

entries.question: When several graph nodes are simultaneously admissible, how often can deterministic software settle the priority before an AI agent is consulted, and what actually limits the exact fallback?

In 15,574 reachable frontier states from a fixed 5–10 node adversarial sample it is oracle-equivalent in 99.28%; all 112 residuals are exactly certified. The exact fallback is then reduced by kernelization, objective-interaction decomposition, and branch-and-bound: representative state counts fall from 8,191 to 12 for independent binary objectives and from 7,714 to 1 for a connected 20-objective cycle, while a 200-node decomposable case remains linear in 100 objective components.

No network, model, or external dependency

Every larger-sample residual is exactly certified by the closure verifier.
Closure verification exactly matches subset-state dynamic programming throughout the exhaustive reachable corpus.
Irrelevant width and forced depth do not inflate closure-search state count in controlled cases.
Objective-alternative scaling remains explicit rather than hidden by an aggregate.
The optimized exact solver matches the reference subset-state oracle on minimum cost and complete oracle-equivalent next-choice sets throughout the exhaustive reachable corpus.
Solver-ladder ablations separately demonstrate kernelization, objective-interaction decomposition, and branch-and-bound reductions.
A 200-node, 100-objective independent case is solved in 100 bounded search states, demonstrating that raw node count is not the controlling parameter.
A fixed connected 80-node, 50-objective stress case remains exactly solvable within 248 bounded search states.

artifacts: Merge gate run 35650473557: exact-head Evidence / Experiment and formal evidence ran the adversarial experiment proof lane including frontier-prioritization and passed.

entries.interpretation: Multiple READY nodes are not themselves an AI prioritization problem. The cheap structural policy settles every exhaustive reachable small-graph frontier and 99.28% of the larger fixed sample; exact verification settles the residuals. The exact fallback can itself be compressed aggressively: kernelization removes dominated/forced structure, objective-interaction decomposition makes independent objective components additive, and branch-and-bound collapses many connected cases. The controlling difficulty is the size and overlap of the remaining interacting objective kernel, not raw graph size. Exceeding a deterministic budget still calls first for stronger deterministic optimization or decomposition, not automatic AI escalation. Heavier exact solvers and parameterized decomposition are explicitly future research rather than acceptance criteria for this experiment.
non_claims: The current heuristic tuple is globally optimal.
The closure verifier is polynomial in arbitrary objective systems.
Every real software objective is machine-readable.
Equal node-selection cost is an adequate production utility model.
All combinatorial optimization should be solved by brute force.
A heuristic result should be trusted without deterministic verification.
No software-engineering task ever requires AI judgment.
Pseudo-Boolean, SAT, CP-SAT, MILP, incremental, or treewidth-aware solvers are required for the current experiment.

design.note: Exploratory deterministic results informed the maintained heuristic and solver ladder. The fixed corpora and exact-oracle checks are reproducible, but the headline thresholds and optimized representation are not claimed as untouched preregistration.

outcome.summary: Across the maintained bounded corpora, cheap deterministic prioritization plus exact closure verification resolves or certifies the modeled READY-frontier choices before AI escalation.

entries.question: Does derived status beat authoritative mutable lifecycle on reconstruction and repair burden?

After semantic-key change or withdrawal of current realization admissibility, the mutable lifecycle control is stale until repaired while all derived implementations recompute directly from facts and current judgments.
Derived implementations require zero durable status-repair writes; the mutable control's repair writes scale with the number of affected materialized lifecycle rows.
After materialized lifecycle erasure, all derived implementations reconstruct from their inputs while the mutable lifecycle control cannot answer until an additional rebuild mechanism restores rows.
The status-free SQLite control preserves the reconstruction and zero-status-write properties, isolating the architectural result from any anti-SQLite or pro-Datalog explanation.
entries.interpretation: The experiment falsifies authoritative mutable lifecycle as the preferred state model for the tested reconstruction and semantic-change requirements. The supported conclusion is derived status, not a particular derived implementation language.

entries.question: Is the current scheduler scaling limit dominated by history/projection reconstruction or by SQLite's serialized authority transaction?
entries.claim: The experiment independently measures history scan, semantic replay, full READY-read latency, and bare multi-process SQLite authority-CAS throughput so the next optimization can target the measured bottleneck rather than inferred architecture.
entries.contrast: Treat poor N-way scheduler scaling as sufficient evidence for distributed authority without decomposing the local transaction path.
environment: Node.js from .node-version
Local filesystem supporting SQLite WAL
Hosted reference run uses GitHub Actions ubuntu-24.04
success_criteria: History scan timing is reported at 10, 100, 1,000, and 5,000 durable commits.
Production replayProjection timing is reported at 1, 8, 32, 64, and 128 valid obligation definitions.
Production deriveReadyWork timing is reported at 1, 8, 32, and 64 definitions.
Bare SQLite authority CAS completes exactly 4,096 appends at 1, 2, 4, and 8 writer processes and reports throughput plus retry pressure.
The interpretation distinguishes storage scan, semantic replay, combined scheduler read, and authority-write serialization.
entries.interpretation: Bare SQLite authority CAS sustained a median 2,387.857 appends/s with one writer and 1,297.630/s with eight, versus the preceding end-to-end scheduler result of about 7.9/s and 2.25/s. History scanning was near-linear at ~5.2 microseconds/commit, while semantic replay and deriveReadyWork grew superlinearly over the tested flat definition sizes. The current dominant scaling limit is repeated reconstruction/projection above SQLite, not bare authority-write capacity. Optimize projection/reconstruction before introducing distributed authority.
non_claims: Absolute benchmark timings are portable across hosts.
Synthetic flat obligation definitions represent every project graph.
SQLite provides distributed HA.
The experiment itself authorizes a production optimization.

design.note: The decomposition question was fixed after an earlier scaling result exposed the bottleneck, while the numeric diagnosis is an observed benchmark result rather than a preregistered threshold.

outcome.summary: The measured current scheduler bottleneck is repeated reconstruction/projection above SQLite rather than bare SQLite authority-write capacity.
